items.title: Bulk Salary Payments in Nigeria: How Businesses Pay Hundreds of Employees Accurately
items.summary: Product Bulk Salary Payments in Nigeria: How Businesses Pay Hundreds of Employees Accurately Oluwakemi Adesina July 7, 2026 Anyone who has managed payroll manually knows how stressful payday can be. For businesses in Nigeria, bulk salary payments make handling payroll for many employees much easier. The main challenge is making the process run smoothly. Paying 300 employees is not just about moving large sums of money. It also means carefully managing data, processes, and compliance. When these are handled well, payroll becomes much simpler. How Bulk Salary Payments in Nigerian Businesses Are Actually Built Instead of thinking of bulk payroll as many transfers at once, think of it as one instruction based on verified data. This instruction is approved once and then processed by the payment system. The process starts with payroll data in the system, including each employee’s name, bank, account number, salary details, and deductions. On payroll day, the platform calculates net pay for everyone. PAYE is deducted in accordance with tax rules. Pension is 8% of basic, housing, and transport. NHF is 2.5% of basic. Other approved deductions are included. The platform then creates a payroll summary showing total gross, total deductions, and total net pay for each employee. The Finance Manager or person in charge reviews the summary. They ensure the headcount matches, the total amount is correct, and there are no unexpected entries. After approval, the platform creates the bulk payment instruction and sends it through bank integration or the NIBSS NIP channel. Each employee receives their net salary at the same time or within the NIP settlement window. The Finance Manager no longer needs to log in to online banking, transfer salaries one by one, or enter account numbers. There is no more waiting for days to learn about failed transactions. The platform handles payments, so the team can focus on approvals. What Makes Bulk Payroll Accurate Accurate bulk payroll starts with onboarding. Each employee’s bank details must be checked before they are added to a payroll run. The way you set up each employee’s salary also affects accuracy. Listing basic, housing, and transport separately allows the system to calculate PAYE, pension, and NHF deductions correctly. If you only enter a single ‘gross salary’ with no breakdown, the system will estimate deductions. Bulk payments then use these estimates for many employees at once. Bulk payment speeds up approvals, but it is still important to check carefully. Before approving, make sure the number of employees matches last month’s count, accounting for new hires and those who have left. Check that the total amount is correct. Look out for unusual changes, such as a doubled salary, a missing deduction, or a new account number for someone already on staff. Spending ten minutes to review can prevent problems later. The Edge Cases That Break Bulk Payroll and How to Handle Them A good bulk payroll process should handle both exceptions and regular monthly payments. These exceptions can often cause problems for businesses if not managed properly. For new employees who start in the middle of the month, someone starting on the 15th should receive half a month’s pay, not a full month. If the platform does not handle pro-rata pay automatically, someone has to manually adjust the bulk file before each run. Manual changes like this can easily lead to mistakes. If employees leave but are still on the payroll, those who resigned on the 20th and whose records were not updated will receive a full month’s salary. It is never easy to recover an overpayment from a former employee. Exit dates should automatically remove people from the payroll run. Failed transactions can happen for many reasons, such as closed accounts, bank problems, or incorrect BVN linking. A payroll platform with real-time monitoring flags failures immediately and explains the reason. The Finance team can then fix them on the same day. Without live tracking, failed transactions might go unnoticed until the employee contacts HR, which could take days. Many agencies and large businesses use different pay cycles, such as monthly, fortnightly, or project-based schedules. If a platform cannot clearly separate these, the finance team has to manage them manually, which defeats the purpose of automation. Bulk Salary Disbursement and Compliance Paying salaries correctly is only one part of payday. The other part is meeting legal requirements, which means your account must be debited for statutory payments soon after employees are paid. PAYE must reach the relevant State IRS by the 10th of the following month, if missed 10% per annum plus MPR interest starts accruing. Pension contributions should be sent to each employee’s PFA within 7 working days. NHF at 2.5% of basic salary goes monthly. These are not separate tasks though. They are the same payroll run, just the part that goes to a regulator instead of an employee. If you use one system for salary payments and handle statutory remittances manually in another, you end up with two separate payroll processes. This can cause late PAYE filings or missed pension deadlines. Bulk payroll software that manages both tasks together solves this problem. Running Bulk Salary Payments with Eazipay If you are a Finance Manager handling payroll for 200 employees in 3 states, payday should be simple. Review once, approve once, and the process is complete. Eazipay allows bulk payment instructions using verified employee data. It calculates net pay for each employee. Your Finance Manager reviews the payroll summary, approves it, and sends the payment via the bank integration. For 200 employees at different banks, the process takes only a few minutes. Failed transactions are displayed on the dashboard with reasons. New employees are paid according to their start date. Employees who leave are removed once their exit is recorded. Different pay schedules can be run separately. Eazipay also handle PAYE remittances, pension contributions, and NHF deductions on a single platform.
